messages:
sam p: quick heads-up — i'm putting a proposal together to converge our ingest schema. plan is to introduce a stable 'route_key' field (string) that replaces reliance on the current numeric route_id for console/telemetry lookups. want quick feedback before i open the RFC/PR :eyes:
maria g: quick Q — why not keep route_id and add route_key as a derived denorm? sounds like duplicate state and backfill headaches
aj chen: +1 to adding route_key but we should avoid a strict copy. prefer dual-write + read-adapter strategy so old consumers keep reading route_id until we cutover.
taylor r: important callout: analytics jobs / dashboards use route_id heavily. any change needs a backfill plan and a rollback story for big p99s. also quotas/billing pipelines are sensitive to key changes.
sam p: agree on all counts. rough plan I sketched: 1) add nullable route_key to ingest record and index it 2) start dual-writing route_key (derived from route metadata) 3) run shadow reads in console/analytics read adapters to validate parity 4) backfill missing route_key for historical rows (chunked) 5) enable read migration + feature flag cutover
lee ng: chunked backfill is fine but we need to estimate io and cpu. our current table is hot — backfill must be rate-limited and prioritized by tenant. also need to update quota evaluation service to accept route_key fallback.
maria g: what's the exact schema change? can you paste the ALTER and index plan so infra can review?
sam p: sure — prototype SQL:```sql
ALTER TABLE telemetry_events ADD COLUMN route_key TEXT; -- nullable
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON telemetry_events (route_key);
-- backfill in batches:
UPDATE telemetry_events SET route_key = r.k
FROM (SELECT id, computed_route_key(id) AS k FROM telemetry_events WHERE route_key IS NULL LIMIT 50000) r
WHERE telemetry_events.id = r.id;
```
(we'd run that in a worker with rate limiting + tenant ordering).
aj chen: instead of UPDATE with JOIN (which bloats WAL), consider INSERT INTO tmp_table SELECT ... then swap partitions or materialize and point read-adapter to tmp. but that is heavier operationally.
taylor r: also add a verification job that computes: pct(route_key IS NULL), mismatch-rate between route_key and lookup(route_id) and cost delta on queries. if mismatch > 0.01% hold the cutover.
sam p: planned checks: daily parity job, histogram of distribution across tenants, sample diff dump for 1000 rows. feature flag gating on per-tenant basis.
lee ng: quota service changes: we should add an interim compatibility function: resolve_route_identity(payload) { if (payload.route_key) return payload.route_key; else return route_lookup(payload.route_id); } then switch evaluation code to use resolve_route_identity. That avoids fragile joins during rollout.
maria g: sounds reasonable. who owns backfill? infra or eng-analytics?
aj chen: eng-platform owns the migration orchestration, but eng-analytics should own verification metrics and dashboards. need a small runbook for throttling/resume.
sam p: i'll draft runbook and PR. proposed timeline: feature branch this week, start dual-write to staging next Tue, limited prod dual-write (10% tenants) in 2 weeks, backfill phased over 3 weeks, cutover at tenant-level in week 6.
taylor r: can we add a canary dashboard tile: p99 latency, query qps, ingest WAL throughput, backfill bytes/sec? show pre/post for the canary tenants.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: sam/p/ingest-route-key-prototype -> staging at 2026-03-25T03:00Z
lee ng: also we need to think about retention compaction. route_key will increase index size; add metric for index bloat and plan for reindex window.
sam p: good catch — will add index-size check to the telemetry alerts and an automatic reindex playbook if >20% growth for 48h.
maria g: any API contract changes for external customers? console API to surface route_key?
aj chen: API change should be additive only. we can include route_key in responses behind a feature flag. don't touch existing route_id field in response until 1+ month after cutover.
sam p: final ask: thumbs if you agree with dual-write + read-adapter + chunked backfill + tenant canary cutover. i'll open RFC + migration PR with the SQL snippets and runbook. :+1:
taylor r: +1 from me, please include rollback commands in the runbook (stop dual-write, point read-adapter back, and run fast nullifier on route_key if we must).
lee ng: +1 — will review index sizing in staging.
maria g: +1, tag me on the PR for dashboards and verification queries.
aj chen: tagging infra on potential WAL/replica lag impact, but otherwise +1.
sam p: thanks all — opening RFC now: https://rdoc.internal/redwood/ingest-route-key-rfc (will post PR link).
